title: Uḫḫamuwa’s ritual
eyebrow: CTH 410 · ritual against dying in the land

dating.label: attested 14th–13th c. BCE
dating.note: The KUB 9.31 and HT 1 copies are dated New Hittite; this is an approximate manuscript date.

purpose: A rite against plague in the land, attributed to Uḫḫamuwa of Arzawa, in which a marked ram is sent away.
attribution: Attributed to Uḫḫamuwa, a man of Arzawa

phases.name: The ram
phases.idea: A marked animal is sent away with a plea for peace.

phases.name: The god’s transport
phases.idea: Materials are brought and a second appeal addresses horses and chariot.

phases.name: The offerings
phases.idea: Three animals take different paths; food and drink follow.

steps.title: Bring a ram
steps.shortDescription: A ram is driven up for the rite.
steps.summary: A ram is driven up for the rite.
steps.evidence: KUB 9.31 reads two(?) rams at this point; the more complete HT 1 has one. The subsequent actions concern one ram.

image.alt: One undecorated ram. Breed, coloration and horn form are illustrative; the text does not specify them.
image.note: One undecorated ram. Breed, coloration and horn form are illustrative; the text does not specify them.

steps.title: Twist the coloured wool
steps.shortDescription: Blue, red, yellow-green, black and white wool are combined.
steps.summary: Blue, red, yellow-green, black and white wool are combined.
steps.evidence: The five colour terms are preserved in KUB 9.31. The exact way the fibres were worked is not described.

image.alt: Dyed fibres converge into a cord; their thickness and dye shades are illustrative.
image.note: Dyed fibres converge into a cord; their thickness and dye shades are illustrative.

steps.title: Make a wool wreath
steps.shortDescription: The combined wool is made into a wreath or ring.
steps.summary: The combined wool is made into a wreath or ring.
steps.evidence: The text names a wool KI-LU-LI; 'wreath' conveys the edited interpretation of its form.

image.alt: A simple circular braid; exact construction is inferred from the term, not preserved as an object.
image.note: A simple circular braid; exact construction is inferred from the term, not preserved as an object.

steps.title: Adorn the ram
steps.shortDescription: The wool wreath is placed on one ram.
steps.summary: The wool wreath is placed on one ram.
steps.evidence: The adorning verb follows the making of the wool object. Its precise position on the animal is not stated.

image.alt: The wreath is shown at the horns for legibility; the precise placement is conjectural.
image.note: The wreath is shown at the horns for legibility; the precise placement is conjectural.

steps.title: Lead the ram toward the enemy road
steps.shortTitle: Lead the ram toward the enemy road
steps.shortDescription: The adorned ram is driven onto the road toward enemy territory.
steps.summary: The adorned ram is driven onto the road toward enemy territory.
steps.evidence: The text specifies a road associated with the enemy; its appearance and exact route are unknown.

image.alt: A closeup of movement. No actual road layout is reconstructed.
image.note: A closeup of movement. No actual road layout is reconstructed.

steps.title: Address the hostile god
steps.shortDescription: An appeal presents the adorned ram and asks the god to be at peace with Ḫatti.
steps.summary: An appeal presents the adorned ram and asks the god to be at peace with Ḫatti.
material: Adorned ram, named in the speech
steps.recipient: Hostile god of the enemy land
steps.evidence: This is a prescribed utterance, not a report that the god visibly accepted the ram. The exact wording varies between witnesses.

image.alt: The crowned ram is the speech's visible referent. The image does not depict the god, a speaker or the requested result.
image.note: The crowned ram is the speech's visible referent. The image does not depict the god, a speaker or the requested result.

steps.title: Drive the ram away
steps.shortDescription: The crowned ram is sent into enemy territory.
steps.summary: The crowned ram is sent into enemy territory.
steps.evidence: This departure is stated after the address. It is distinct from bringing the ram onto the road.

image.alt: The ram walks away; no specific border, settlement or road is invented.
image.note: The ram walks away; no specific border, settlement or road is invented.

steps.title: Bring fodder and fat
steps.shortDescription: Fodder for the god's horses and sheep fat are brought.
steps.summary: Fodder for the god's horses and sheep fat are brought.
steps.recipient: Horses and chariot named in the following speech
steps.evidence: Bringing the materials is stated. Feeding horses or greasing a chariot is wished for in the subsequent utterance, not described here as performed.

image.alt: Only the named materials are shown; a container is deliberately omitted.
image.note: Only the named materials are shown; a container is deliberately omitted.

steps.title: Address the god about his horses
steps.shortTitle: Address the god about his horses
steps.shortDescription: The speech asks that the horses eat, the chariot be greased, and the god turn back toward his land.
steps.summary: The speech asks that the horses eat, the chariot be greased, and the god turn back toward his land.
material: Fodder and fat, named in the speech
steps.evidence: These are wishes within an utterance. The text does not say the horses were actually fed or the chariot actually greased.

image.alt: The image visualizes the named horses/chariot as referents of speech, not as an attested scene of feeding or greasing.
image.note: The image visualizes the named horses/chariot as referents of speech, not as an attested scene of feeding or greasing.

steps.title: Bring a goat and two sheep
steps.shortTitle: Bring a goat and two sheep
steps.shortDescription: A billy goat and two sheep are brought into the rite.
steps.summary: A billy goat and two sheep are brought into the rite.
steps.patient: One billy goat and two sheep
steps.evidence: The number and animal categories are explicit in this witness.

image.alt: One goat and two sheep, with no invented accessories or ceremonial setting.
image.note: One goat and two sheep, with no invented accessories or ceremonial setting.

steps.title: Dedicate the goat to the Seven
steps.shortTitle: Dedicate the goat to the Seven
steps.shortDescription: The billy goat is assigned to the Seven (Sebettu).
steps.summary: The billy goat is assigned to the Seven (Sebettu).
steps.evidence: The recipient and animal are named. The precise physical gesture is not described.

image.alt: The goat alone is shown; no image of the divine recipients or invented gesture.
image.note: The goat alone is shown; no image of the divine recipients or invented gesture.

steps.title: Dedicate one sheep to the Sun-god
steps.shortTitle: Dedicate one sheep to the Sun-god
steps.shortDescription: One sheep is assigned to the Sun-god.
steps.summary: One sheep is assigned to the Sun-god.
steps.evidence: This assignment is present in KUB 9.31; the published English draft notes a variant in another witness.

image.alt: One sheep in natural light. The deity and a specific gesture are not depicted.
image.note: One sheep in natural light. The deity and a specific gesture are not depicted.

steps.title: Kill the remaining sheep
steps.evidence: The text names the killing but not an implement or method.

image.alt: A single anonymous hand and plain bronze blade make the act legible. The text does not specify a knife, cutting method, or precise position; all are illustrative.
image.note: A single anonymous hand and plain bronze blade make the act legible. The text does not specify a knife, cutting method, or precise position; all are illustrative.

steps.title: Cook the sheep
steps.evidence: The verb states cooking but not vessel, fuel or method.

image.alt: A plausible plain ceramic cooking vessel is illustrative only; its use is not specified in this line.
image.note: A plausible plain ceramic cooking vessel is illustrative only; its use is not specified in this line.

steps.title: Bring food and drink
steps.shortDescription: Cheese, sour bread, wine, beer and fruit are brought, along with named vessels.
steps.summary: Cheese, sour bread, wine, beer and fruit are brought, along with named vessels.
steps.evidence: The vessel names survive; their exact shapes and the fruit species are not settled here.

image.alt: A restrained selection of generic food and ceramic vessels; fruit species and vessel profiles are illustrative.
image.note: A restrained selection of generic food and ceramic vessels; fruit species and vessel profiles are illustrative.

steps.title: Prepare them for the road god
steps.shortTitle: Prepare them for the road god
steps.shortDescription: The gathered provisions are prepared for the god of the road.
steps.summary: The gathered provisions are prepared for the god of the road.
steps.evidence: The text says the provisions are prepared for this god; the placement or arrangement is unspecified.

image.alt: A schematic still life of provisions, not a reconstruction of an attested altar or gesture.
image.note: A schematic still life of provisions, not a reconstruction of an attested altar or gesture.
